0.text: Emotional exhaustion is often the result of prolonged stress and a lack of resources for recovery. Taking regular breaks, pursuing hobbies, and having support from family and friends can significantly help in managing this state.
0.fact: A Gallup survey of employees found that 23% of respondents experience burnout always or very often, while another 44% experience it sometimes.

1.text: Physical activity and proper nutrition play a key role in maintaining energy levels and preventing feelings of fatigue.
1.fact: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has spoken many times about the importance of adequate rest and sleep for maintaining productivity and preventing exhaustion. He maintains that getting at least eight hours of sleep a day helps him stay energetic and effective.

2.text: Planning your morning can help reduce stress and boost motivation. Rituals such as exercising, meditating, or reading can make your morning more enjoyable.
2.fact: Apple CEO Tim Cook is known for his early rising (around 4:30 a.m.). However, he emphasizes the importance of good nighttime sleep and regular physical exercise for maintaining energy and motivation.

3.text: Emotional intelligence training can help leaders and employees understand each other better and work more effectively. This can include courses on active listening, conflict management, and empathy development.
3.fact: Emotional intelligence (EQ) plays a key role in team management and workplace success. According to TalentSmart, research shows that 90% of top performers possess a high level of emotional intelligence.

4.text: Empathy and personal attention from leadership can significantly reduce employee turnover. A study published in Harvard Business Review showed that employees who feel supported and noticed by their managers are four times less likely to leave the company.
4.fact: Tesla and SpaceX founder Elon Musk is known for his demanding and intense style. Some employees have noted that his management style can be harsh and lack a personal touch, leading to stress and burnout within the team.

5.text: Psychological practices such as meditation, yoga, and mindfulness techniques can help maintain emotional balance and increase energy levels.
5.fact: Virgin Group founder Richard Branson is known for his enthusiasm and energy. He often emphasizes the importance of a positive mindset and energy for achieving success in both business and personal life. Branson claims that a positive attitude helps him overcome difficulties and inspire his team.

6.text: Conflict management training can include developing skills in active listening, empathy, and the ability to find compromises. Courses and workshops on these topics can be highly beneficial for employees at all levels.
6.fact: Effective conflict resolution can significantly boost team productivity. A Harvard Business Review study showed that companies that manage conflict successfully have 30% higher productivity.

7.text: Psychotherapy and consulting with a psychologist can be very helpful for those experiencing feelings of being overwhelmed and apathy. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is often used to treat depression and burnout.

8.text: Feedback and recognition from colleagues and management can strengthen your confidence in the importance of your work. Regularly recognizing employee achievements helps increase motivation and job satisfaction.
8.fact: Job satisfaction is linked to improved performance. According to Harvard Business Review, employees who see the value in their work are 21% more productive and 22% more profitable for the company.

9.text: Neuroscience research has shown that when people show empathy, their brains activate the same areas as they do for physical pain. This means that emotional connections can truly be deep and meaningful.
9.fact: Bridgewater Associates founder Ray Dalio is known for his philosophy of “radical transparency” and honesty in the workplace. He believes that openly discussing problems and mistakes helps improve team relationships and increase efficiency.

10.text: Research shows that maintaining a work-life balance can significantly reduce stress levels and prevent cynicism. Companies like Basecamp actively promote shorter workweeks and minimizing overtime to improve employee well-being.
10.fact: Martin Seligman’s work in positive psychology shows that developing traits such as gratitude and optimism can significantly improve emotional well-being and reduce cynicism.

11.text: Research in positive psychology, such as the work of Martin Seligman, shows that optimism and belief in the future can significantly improve quality of life and help in achieving goals.
11.fact: In some countries, such as Sweden, there is the concept of “fika” — a mandatory coffee and social break that helps reduce stress and prevent burnout.

12.text: Immersing yourself in hobbies or personal projects can provide a sense of satisfaction and balance out negative work-related emotions. Famous entrepreneurs, such as Richard Branson, are actively involved in various personal projects that bring them joy and inspiration.

13.text: Jack Ma, the founder of a major internet company, was once a proponent of the “996” work model (9 a.m. to 9 p.m., 6 days a week). However, he later admitted that such a schedule can be harmful to the health of both employees and the organization as a whole.

14.text: Research shows that burnout can be “contagious” in work environments, spreading from one employee to another.

15.text: The concept of a “digital detox” — a period of complete disconnection from electronic devices — is becoming increasingly popular as a way to combat information overload and burnout.
15.fact: Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg is known for taking long vacations and disconnecting from social media. He believes these breaks help him maintain the energy and inspiration needed for his work.

16.text: The concept of “psychological safety” in teams was developed by Harvard Business School professor Amy Edmondson. She argues that it is a key factor in team effectiveness.
16.fact: According to the Society for Human Resource Management, 61% of employees believe that trust between workers and management is very important for job satisfaction.

17.text: The concept of “flow”, described by psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi, explains a state of complete immersion in an activity, accompanied by a sense of energy and enjoyment.
17.fact: Google uses a “20% time” rule, allowing employees to spend one-fifth of their working time on projects of their own choosing, which boosts creativity and engagement.

18.text: According to the Pew Research Center, 30% of Americans view their work as a calling, 44% as a career, and 24% simply as a way to make a living.
18.fact: TOMS Shoes uses a “One for One” model, where they donate a pair of shoes for every pair sold, giving employees a sense that their work provides real benefit.

19.text: The Japanese concept of “ikigai” describes the intersection of what you love, what you are good at, what the world needs, and what you can be paid for. It is considered a key to job satisfaction.
19.fact: Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus founded Grameen Bank to provide microloans to the poor. He often speaks about the importance of creating “social business” to solve global problems.

20.text: In Sweden, some companies are experimenting with a 6-hour workday to increase productivity and reduce burnout. Preliminary results show an increase in employee energy and motivation.
20.fact: In 2008, Oprah Winfrey admitted that she was experiencing burnout and a loss of interest in her show, which led to her decision to end it a few years later.

21.text: Google offers its employees a course called “Search Inside Yourself,” which teaches mindfulness and emotional intelligence skills to better manage stress and emotions at work.
21.fact: According to the World Health Organization, depression and anxiety cost the global economy $1 trillion a year in lost productivity.

22.text: In psychology, the term “emotional vampirism” describes people who drain the energy of those around them, often by offloading their own problems onto others.
22.fact: Some companies, such as Zappos, implement a “holacracy” system — a management model where responsibility is distributed among self-organizing teams rather than being concentrated in managers.

low.text: Your productivity level is currently stable and within a comfortable zone. You might feel tired sometimes, but overall, you’re managing to maintain a healthy rhythm and a good balance between work and rest. This helps you preserve your energy, motivation, and mental well-being. Keep being kind to yourself and maintaining this balance.
low.title: High productivity

middle.text: Your productivity has dipped slightly, perhaps due to an increased workload or a lack of recovery. It’s not critical yet, and you’re still able to work and find satisfaction in your tasks. However, it might be helpful to focus on your work-life balance right now to maintain steady energy and emotional stability.
middle.title: Reduced productivity

high.text: Your resources may be significantly depleted. You might have been under high pressure for a long time or working on tasks that don’t bring you satisfaction. This can affect your motivation, mood, and sense of purpose at work. Now is a particularly important time to slow down, recover, and prioritize your well-being. Seeking support, resting, and reassessing your workload will help you regain energy and resilience.
high.title: Close to burnout

text: Do you often feel tired, lose interest in your work, or struggle to recharge your energy?
This test will help determine if you’re showing signs of emotional exhaustion and how balanced your workload and rest are.
Your answers will show how your resources are doing right now and whether you should make changes to support your productivity and well-being.
